to: Category Labs project owner via the HN-listed application channel
subject: Five-minute Rust demo for Category Labs — Senior Software Engineer (C++ / Rust): https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/category-labs/a0af69a1-8a77-4bda-b5...
body:
Hello Category Labs team,

Saw your Senior Software Engineer (C++/Rust) post via the July 2026 HN Who's Hiring thread and the Ashby link. C++/Rust as a joint hiring signal usually means either a system with a hot native core that has to interop with safer glue, or a rewrite in progress; either way a pilot has to be small, cheap to reason about, and provably regression-free before anyone lets an outside contributor touch a mutex. That's the wedge for a bounded paid pilot: I take one narrow FFI or IPC seam (Rust wrapping a C++ library, or a Rust CLI shelling into your existing tools), and ship a deterministic slice with property-style tests plus a JSON receipt of what ran, so any future breakage points at the seam that moved rather than 'somebody's Rust'.

Proposed first milestone (paid, fixed-scope):
1. Reproduce one representative Rust<->C++ or Rust CLI seam on synthetic inputs.
2. Add the property/refused-input tests + exportable receipt.
3. Hand over the code, a short runbook, and one acceptance check Category Labs can re-run.

Proof: https://hfo-games.pages.dev/ ships 21 live browser games and https://github.com/TTaoGaming/hfo-gen-133 exposes the append-only receipts and operator-gated effect model behind that cadence. I'm proposing bounded integration labor, not the Senior SWE seat.

If a small Rust/C++ seam is real for Category Labs, book 15 minutes: {{OPERATOR_BOOKING_LINK}}. If not, no follow-up.

— TTaoGaming
https://github.com/TTaoGaming
